adjudication_records.issue_text: mixins.scss align-items(baseline) forwards baseline to -ms-flex-align and -webkit-box-align where it's invalid, dropping the declaration on IE10/old Android WebKit and stretching the badge out of line with the bullet

The finding claims `baseline` is invalid for those prefixed properties, but the diff itself does not show that: `baseline` is a standard/recognized value for both old `box-align` and `-ms-flex-align` implementations. adjudication_records.issue_text: -ms-align-items on line 119 is a nonexistent fabricated vendor property, dead code in the shipped mixin

In the same mixin it already sets the IE/old-MS flexbox property `-ms-flex-align: $alignment;`, so `-ms-align-items` is at best redundant and likely an invalid/nonstandard vendor property, making it dead/unused CSS rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: header.scss .contents is a flex row with no flex-wrap, so on narrow screens panel/login buttons compress or overflow instead of wrapping as the old float layout allowed

adjudication.rationale: In `header.scss`, `.contents` was changed from a float-based layout (`.title { float: left; }` and `.panel { float: right; }`) to a flex container via `@include flexbox()` with `@include align-items(center)`. No `flex-wrap` is added, so the flex container will default to `nowrap`. That means its children (including the right-aligned `.panel` now using `margin-left: auto`) will stay on one line and are more likely to shrink/overflow instead of wrapping/stacking on narrow widths, whereas the prior float layout could allow the right-floated panel to drop below when space is insufficient.

adjudication_records.issue_text: header.scss legacy 2009 flexbox (-webkit-box/-moz-box) does not honor margin-left: auto, so .panel is not right-aligned on old WebKit/Firefox

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces `float: right;` on `.panel` with `margin-left: auto;` and sets `.contents` to `@include flexbox()` (which emits legacy `display: -webkit-box;` / `display: -moz-box;` before modern flex). In older 2009 box implementations, auto margins are not reliably supported for main-axis alignment the way modern flexbox is, so this change can plausibly break right-alignment in those legacy engines where the previous float-based layout worked.

adjudication_records.issue_text: @include order(3) on .panel in header.scss:36-41 hard-codes DOM-position knowledge; future children added to .contents will silently render misordered between .title (default order) and order-2/3 elements, and margin-left:auto alone already achieves panel right-alignment making order(3) unnecessary coupling

The new `padding: 0 1.5%` on `.small-action-desc` affects only the *internal* padding of the description box, not its position relative to the avatar, so it does not cause the text to underlap the avatar the way the old `padding-left: 4em` (used as an offset in non-flex layout) might have. adjudication_records.issue_text: Making .small-action a flex row with align-items: center changes wrapping behavior for long descriptions due to min-width: auto on flex items

This can realistically change how `.small-action-desc` (and other children like `.topic-avatar`) shrink/wrap compared to the prior non-flex layout, potentially causing long descriptions to overflow or wrap differently unless `min-width: 0`/wrapping rules are added on the flex item.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Establishing flex layout on .contents changes layout semantics of all children (margin collapsing, width as flex-basis, floats ignored), silently breaking stylesheets relying on block formatting context

This indeed changes formatting-context semantics for all direct children of `.contents` (floats no longer apply, flex sizing rules apply, margin-collapsing differs). However, the claim that it "silently" breaks other stylesheets relying on block layout can’t be verified from this diff alone; it’s a real, diff-grounded risk/concern rather than a proven defect here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic-post.scss:277-280 — unrequested visual redesign of `.small-action-desc`: deleting `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` and margin/padding values changes spacing of small-action components with no rationale in a performance PR

adjudication_records.issue_text: header.scss / topic.scss — adding CSS `order` to `.extra-info-wrapper` and `.panel` causes visual order to diverge from DOM/tab order, changing accessibility for assistive tech and keyboard users as an unapproved side effect of a perf optimization

Using CSS `order` can change visual order independently of DOM order, which can create an accessibility mismatch for keyboard/assistive tech users. The PR diff doesn’t show the full flex context for `.extra-info-wrapper` or the DOM structure, so the exact impact isn’t fully verifiable here, but the concern is diff-grounded and specific to the added `order` usage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: badges.css.scss:52-59 — replacing modern flexbox declarations (`display: inline-flex; align-items: baseline`) with legacy vendor-prefix mixins including non-standard `-moz-box` and `-ms-align-items` regresses the accepted clean, standards-based badge styling

The diff still outputs the modern unprefixed `inline-flex` and `align-items`, so an actual styling regression is not verifiable from the diff alone, but the introduction of obsolete/non-standard declarations is a concrete, diff-grounded maintainability/compatibility concern rather than a proven bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: mixins.scss flexbox(), inline-flex(), align-items(), and order() mixins emit dead legacy vendor-prefixed syntax (-moz-box, -ms-flexbox, -webkit-box-ordinal-group) that is silently ignored by modern browsers, obscuring which declaration actually applies when debugging in devtools

While not a functional bug (it may be intentional for older browser support), these extra declarations can be ignored by many modern browsers and can make it harder to tell in devtools which declaration is actually taking effect, so it’s a concrete maintainability/debuggability concern grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: order(3) on .panel may interact with DOM source order of .title, causing visual-layout regression

adjudication.rationale: In `header.scss`, `.contents` is converted to a flex container (`@include flexbox()`), and `.panel` is given `@include order(3)` plus `margin-left: auto`, while `.title` no longer has `float: left` and has no explicit `order`. In a flex context, `order` can change visual ordering relative to DOM order and other flex items (default order is 0), so introducing `order(3)` could indeed alter where `.panel` appears compared to `.title` depending on the markup and any other ordered items. The diff alone can’t prove a regression, but it does introduce a real ordering/behavioral risk grounded in the change.
